key_insight: SJ-KAN analytically propagates spatial derivatives through a compact spectral network, achieving comparable or better flow-solution accuracy with up to 47× fewer parameters and 8.2× faster training per epoch than tested baselines.
engineering_relevance: The approach could reduce the computational cost of physics-informed incompressible flow solvers, including high-Reynolds-number cavity simulations without reference data.
method: Embed coordinates in Chebyshev bases and precompute their derivatives at collocation points.
Linearly compress the bases into latent features, then map them to flow variables with a single nonlinear CKAN layer.
Compute PDE spatial derivatives analytically; reserve automatic differentiation for loss gradients with respect to weights.
evidence_signal: Three SJ-KAN variants were evaluated on Taylor–Green vortex and lid-driven cavity benchmarks, including cavity Reynolds numbers of 100–10,000, against AD-based PIKAN and standard PINN baselines.
watch_item: Evidence is limited to the reported benchmarks; performance on complex geometries and broader flow regimes remains unestablished.
paper_title: SPARK: Spectral Preconditioned Analytic Residual Kolmogorov Arnold Networks for incompressible Navier Stokes equations
